why: Ref: caroled song; whistled syllables ~2-3.5 kHz, peak ~2.8 kHz; existing values sound.

Slurred whistle series 1.5-6.5 kHz, trills faster; au = established Hawaii introduction. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Perch-coo: main notes ~390 Hz, rising 2nd note ~650 Hz; harmonics weak.
Ref: fee-bee song, pure tones ~4.0 then ~3.3 kHz; broadband chick-a-dee call excluded.
Ref: caw series; harsh but harmonic, energy ~0.5-3 kHz peaking ~1.4 kHz.
Ref: harsh 'jay' jeer call given in short series; broadband ~1-5 kHz.
Song mixes intro notes, buzz and trill ~1.5-7.5 kHz; peak ~3.5-4 kHz.
Bubbling cascade of rapid trilled phrases ~2.5-7 kHz; sy covers Southern House Wren split.
Flute-like ee-oh-lay phrases ~1.5-4 kHz plus high terminal trill.
Ref: 'who-cooks-for-you' hoot series; near-tonal, ~0.3-0.8 kHz.
Ref: male yodel; dominant ~1.65-2.0 kHz (Mager et al. 2007), harmonic. +eu: Iceland, winter coasts.
Ref: strident 'kill-deee' calls; Hz unverified. +sa: resident Peru/Chile race, NW South America winterers.
Rich whistled song ~1.5-4 kHz; winters regularly in Colombia/Venezuela/Ecuador.
Long canary-like twittering warble ~2-7 kHz.
Soft low warbled whistles mostly 2-4 kHz; prior range too wide, fdom high.
Ref: hoarse descending kee-eeer scream; energy mostly ~1.5-4 kHz (estimate, not measured).
Ref: territorial drum ~16 beats/s; broadband, substrate-dependent spectrum.
Pure whistled 'Oh-sweet-Canada' notes ~2.8-4.8 kHz; absolute pitch varies between individuals.
Ref: harsh low 'frahnk' croak; broadband, values unverified.
No song; ref: chip/chatter calls ~2-8 kHz. Wing hum is not vocal.
Loud rolling 'tea-kettle' whistled syllables repeated ~3-5/s, ~2-5 kHz.
Ref: song, two notes then trill; f corrected: it is the song, not a call.
Varied warble ~1-7 kHz; f fixed: '100+ species per bout' unsupported, mimicry sparse.
Genuine Cedar Waxwing. No song; ref: thin trilled 'sreee' call ~7-9 kHz.
'Conk-la-ree': notes then buzzy trill ~2-5 kHz. Repertoires are ~2-8, not 15.

Long jumbled warble ending buzzy ~2-6 kHz; au = abundant established Hawaii introduction. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Ref: musical trill ~3-6 kHz; prior fmin and fdom too low.
Bright 'sweet-sweet' whistled series ~3.5-7.5 kHz; IOC splits N American birds as aestiva.
Ref: deep hoot series; male ~0.25-0.4 kHz, female higher; nothing vocal below ~200 Hz.

Mimetic phrases each repeated 3-6 times, 1-8 kHz; au = established Hawaii introduction. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Paired sharp whistled notes ~3-8 kHz.
Ref: crescendo 'teacher' series ~3-7 kHz; w set to canonical article title.
Ref: high chippering twitter. f fixed: roosts in chimneys nightly. Winters western Amazonia.
Ref: rolling bugle, fundamental ~0.6-1 kHz with rich harmonics; breeds NE Siberia.
Fluty warble ~1.5-3.5 kHz then soft twitter; NW Africa resident; introduced Australia/NZ.
Varied liquid high phrases ~2-8 kHz; breeds NW Africa and W Asia/Siberia.
Varied phrases repeated 2-4 times ~1.5-6 kHz; Siberian breeder, N Africa winterer, NZ/Australia introduced.
Descending trill phrases plus flourish ~2-7 kHz; NZ introduced; N African birds now split.
Ref: 'tea-cher' two-note whistles ~3-6 kHz; NW Africa resident.
High 'tsee-tsee' then trill ~4-8 kHz; NW African birds are C. teneriffae.
Loud rapid trills mostly 4-8 kHz, peak nearer 6 kHz; Maghreb resident.
Ref: 'cu-coo' ~0.65 then ~0.53 kHz, near-pure tones; winters in Africa.
Sustained rapid varied warble ~2-7 kHz; winters N Africa; introduced NZ/SE Australia.
Twittering warble with creaky rattle ~2-7 kHz; winters S America, New Guinea/N Australia.
IOC name. Warble ending in rich fluting ~2-5 kHz; breeds W Asia.
Ref: 'chiff-chaff' tonal downslurred notes ~3.5-6.5 kHz; winters N and W Africa.
Tinkling twittering song ~3-8 kHz; Maghreb resident; introduced Australia/NZ and Uruguay/Argentina.
Ref: 3-note coo ~0.45-0.6 kHz. f dates corrected (reached Britain 1955). Introduced N America.
Ref: male hoot, first note ~0.75-0.85 kHz; ke-wick reaches ~2.5 kHz; W Asia.
Rapid repeated notes ~4-7 kHz plus drawn-out end note; W Siberia; introduced NZ.
Whistles, clicks, rattles, mimicry 1-7 kHz; W/C Asia; introduced South Africa, Argentina.
Ref: 5-note coo, elements ~0.23-0.65 kHz per published sonogram; Maghreb, W/C Asia.
Varied whistles, crescendos, rapid 'jug' series ~1.5-8 kHz; h fixed: breeds north to England/Poland.
Ref: shrill scream, fundamental ~4-6.5 kHz, harmonic ~8-9 kHz.
Species name ('pied' = UK race). Twittering song of call-like notes ~3-7 kHz; winters Africa.
Hurried high scratchy warble ~3-8 kHz; breeds Turkey/Caucasus/N Iran; introduced NZ.
Twittering trills plus wheezy 'dzweee' ~2-6 kHz; Maghreb; introduced Australia/NZ.
No real song; ref: thin 'see' and trilled 'tsirrup' contact calls ~5-9 kHz.
Loud fluty short phrases ~2-4.5 kHz; NW Africa resident.
Ref: 2-note crow, harmonic, fundamental ~0.8-1 kHz (Heinz & Gysel 1970). Introduced NA/NZ/Hawaii.
Ref: wheezy 'pee-wit' call; Hz unverified. Winters N Africa. Etymology corrected (hleapewince).
Very high cyclic 'zeedle' song plus flourish ~6-9 kHz.
Fast twittering warble ~2-7 kHz; breeds W/C Asia.
Ref: laughing chorus, harsh harmonic cackles ~0.5-3 kHz; values unverified.
Ref: carolling, flutey plus harsh elements ~1-4 kHz, peak ~2 kHz.
Ref: harsh broadband screech; energy ~0.5-3.5 kHz.
Shrill screeching chatter; split from T. haematodus, which GBIF may still use.
Ref: high reeling trill song ~4-9 kHz.
Ref: male long whistle plus rapid whip-crack sweep, female answers; Hz unverified.
Ref: harsh repeated chatter and alarm notes; values unverified.
Ref: 'sweet-pretty-creature' tonal song; harsh chatter also common.
Ref: shrill 'chet' contact calls, higher than cockatoo screech (estimate).
Flute-like song mostly ~1-3 kHz; fdom lowered (estimate).
Ref: low pulsed 'oom-oom-oom' series; values unverified.
Song: varied loud whistled phrases with harsh notes and mimicry; existing range plausible, unchanged.
Song: short liquid whistled phrases centred ~2.5 kHz; established Miami, Mauritius and Réunion populations.
Song: varied gurgles, croaks, whistles and mimicry; established introduced population in Florida.
Reference: shrill whistled 'tzee' flight call; breeds NW Africa, ranges east to New Guinea and Solomons.

Song: long low whistle ~1–1.5 kHz then 'hokekyo' to ~4 kHz; established in Hawaii since 1929. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Reference: drawn-out broadband screech, peak ~3 kHz; a single long note, so no note rate.
Reference: loud harmonic 'may-awe' scream, fundamental ~1 kHz; long-established feral birds in NZ and Hawaii.
Reference: male's rising 'ko-el' series; Australasian birds are Pacific Koel (E. orientalis).
Song: fluty whistles ~1.2–3 kHz; kunang-kunang means firefly; breeds East Asia, not South Asia.
Reference: soft three-note coo ~0.5–0.6 kHz; HBW splits western S. suratensis.
Reference: duetted goose-like honking 'kank-kank-kank'; IOC and Clements moved it to Icthyophaga.

Reference: crow, harmonic with harsh parts; Polynesian-introduced populations persist on Pacific islands. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
2015 split: T. paradisi is the S/C Asian species; rolling whistled song, frequencies unverified.

Song: long, varied, rich fluty phrases with mimicry; established on Kauai and Oahu. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Reference: monotonous tonal 'tuk' hoots ~1.2 kHz, about two per second.
Reference: ringing yelping 'weee-ah, kyow-kow-kow' with overtones; IOC moved it to Icthyophaga.
Reference: loud nasal 'haa-haa-ha-de-dah' flight calls; frequencies not verified.
Reference: 'kuk-COORR-uk' coo; Afrikaans name 'Werk-harder' unsupported; Wikipedia title is Ring-necked dove.
Song: varied metallic, harsh and whistled notes with extensive mimicry.
Song: varied melodious whistled phrases with mimicry; frequencies not verified.
Reference: wild flock whistles and harsh screeches; mixed texture, values not verified.
Song: long mix of buzzy swizzles, chatters and whistles; invasive established population on Hispaniola.
Reference: harsh croaking 'kraak' caw.
Reference: harsh rasping 'rak-rak' calls and cackles in display flight.
Song: brief jumbled chatter ending in a wheeze; values not verified.
Reference: nasal piping 'yip-purr' and 'kek' series; also resident in southwestern Arabia.
Reference: hollow accelerating 'wok-wok-wok' clucking display, energy near 1 kHz.
Song: Turdus-style fluty caroling phrases.
Reference: loud 'kis-ka-dee' call, pitched with strong overtones.
Reference: deep guttural croaking 'grrek', repeated about once per second.
No song: chip/chatter calls are most recorded; winters in Mexico, not South America.
Reference: high twittering 'pip-pip-pip-peeeerr'; frequencies not verified.
Song: slurred whistles then dialect-specific trill; resident from southern Mexico and Hispaniola southward.
Reference: explosive whistled 'pi-pi-yo' call; frequency values not verified.
Reference: low hollow double hoot 'hoo-doo' ~0.5 kHz; old fact garbled the tail-wag signal.
Reference: harsh squealing and grunting lek calls.
Song: repeated harmonic 'chirrup' chirps; Brooklyn releases were dozens of birds, not eight.
Reference: low bow-coo; beak-magnetite compass disproved (Treiber 2012); Monet/Picasso from Watanabe 1995.
Reference: deep resonant croak; breeds across North Africa.
Reference: harsh broadband 'kak-kak-kak' cackle.
Reference: series of whistled 'kyew' notes; winters widely in South America; IOC splits Eastern Osprey.
Reference: harsh 'kee-arr' call; breeds Arctic Asia, regular passage off Africa and South America.
Reference: bill-clattering, rapid broadband clacks; adults largely voiceless.
Reference: tremulous whinnying whistle 'pee-errr'; 'roosts of millions' unsupported.
Reference: male's rising mewing hoot ~1 kHz, repeated every few seconds; established in New Zealand.
Song: clear whistled 'peter-peter-peter'.
Song: rapid nasal 'wha-wha-wha' series with harmonics.
Reference: rolling burry 'kwirr' call, its most-heard vocalization; repetition rate variable.
Reference: long 'wick-wick-wick' call series at about 7 notes per second.
Reference: loud wild 'wuk-wuk-wuk' call series; HBW/BirdLife place it in Hylatomus.
Song: burry 'fee-bee' with energy mostly 3–6 kHz.
Song: slow slurred whistled 'pee-a-wee'; winters in northern South America.
Song: dry mechanical trill, energy ~4–7 kHz.
Song: whistled intro, buzzy notes and trill; 'two weeks awake' overstated (Rattenborg 2004).
Song: liquid twittering chirps and gurgles.
Song: throaty gurgling croaks and chortles; winters in Amazonian South America.
Song: squeaky, creaking, grating twitters; winters in southern South America.
Entry is Bohemian (Cedar listed separately); its 'sirrr' trill is lower, buzzier than Cedar's.
Song: low bubbling gurgles ending in very high whistle; spectral peak uncertain.
Song: squeaky grating 'readle-eak' burst.
Reference: female's descending quack series; breeds NW Africa, established in NZ, Australia, South Africa.
Reference: two-syllable harmonic honk; long established in New Zealand.
Reference: female's squealing 'oo-eek' flush call.
Reference: low harsh croak 'kraak'.
Reference: loud dry rattle; winters to northern South America.
Reference: shrill 'klee-klee-klee'; vole-urine UV claim comes from Eurasian Kestrel and is contested.
Reference: harsh 'cak-cak-cak'; 2024 Accipiter split moved cooperii to Astur.
Reference: broadband hiss; also hunts by sight, so 'by smell alone' overstated.
Reference: male gobble, a rapid guttural rattle; well established in New Zealand.
Song: rich 'churry-churry-chorry-chorry'; winters to Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador.
Song: whistled 'witchety' triplets, energy mainly 3–6 kHz.
Song: high thin 'tsee-tsee-tsweeo' notes; winters in northern South America.
Song: burry, hoarse robin-like phrases; winters in northwestern South America.
Song: rich, fast robin-like whistled warble; winters to northern South America.
Song: repeated 'teechu' whistles ~4-8 kHz, peak ~6 kHz; Atlas populations breed in NW Africa.
Song: repeated 'schip/tju' chevron notes; existing values plausible but unverified.
Song: loud 'pee-pee' whistles ~2-4 kHz, slow or fast-trilled; resident in Moroccan Atlas/Rif.
Song: thin descending accelerating series ~5-9 kHz ending in flourish; values fit.
Song: whistled intro, 'tru-tru' notes, then variable scratchy/mimetic flourish; values reasonable.
Song: short squeaky scratchy warbled phrases; breeds Turkey/Caucasus, winters Middle East.
Curruca genus (IOC/Clements). Song: brief fast scratchy warble; frequencies unverified.
Song: soft descending cadence of whistled notes, ~2.5-3 s; values fit.
Song: long varied chatter with churrs, trills, mimicry; lower churrs; breeds east to C Siberia.
Song: rhythmic chattering, syllables repeated 2-4 times; breeds W/C Asia and Middle East.
Song: accelerating 'zi-zi-zi' series, lower than Goldcrest, peak ~7 kHz; breeds NW Africa.
Song: slow plaintive 'piu-piu-piu' pure whistles ~3-4 kHz, unlike Marsh Tit.
Reference: soft piping 'peu' call (song quiet, rarely heard); narrow whistle ~2 kHz.
Reference: sharp 'tzik'/'tsii' calls (song rarely heard), measured ~6-9 kHz; NW Africa race buvryi.
Song: rattling 'chet-chet' flight trills plus buzzy notes; AOS/Clements 2024 lumped redpolls.
Song: fast twitter ending in loud wheeze ~4 kHz; stop copying Goldfinch triple.
Reference: harsh 'fraank' flight call, low broadband; values fit.
American birds split as Common Gallinule. Reference: explosive 'kurruk' croak, mostly 1-3 kHz.
Split 2011 on vocal differences. Reference: decelerating series of nasal clucks.
Reference: loud short 'kowk'/'pitt' calls given singly; resident across North Africa.
Reference: shrill rapid 'kee-kee-kee' series; values fit.
Reference: 'kek-kek-kek' chatter near nest; mostly silent, little data.
Reference: descending mewing 'peee-yow'; Steppe Buzzards winter in E and S Africa.
Reference: laughing 'yaffle' series; ranges into Turkey/Caucasus/Iran; Iberian birds split by IOC.
Reference: short territorial drum; spectrum substrate-dependent. Resident in NW Africa.
Reference: liquid rolled 'prruip' flight call; rechecked, no firm basis to change fdom.
Song: descending fluty phrase then twittering chatter; fluty part dominates ~3 kHz.
Reference: harsh 'chack-chack' call (song rarely heard away from breeding grounds).
Song: Great Tit-like 'tsupi-tsupi' two-note phrases; similar pitch to Great Tit.
Song: short liquid chattering phrases; bulbul songs centre lower than template.
Song: repeated metallic chirps; established introduced populations in SE Australia and St Louis area.

Reference: varied harsh and whistled calls with mimicry; introduced, established on Guam and Rota. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]

Reference: shrill 'kee-ak' screech; large established feral population on Kauai, Hawaii. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]

Reference: bubbling whistled 'be-care-ful'; mid-low pitch. Invasive on Hawaii, Fiji, Samoa, Tonga. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Song: short whistled warbling phrases; formerly genus Saxicoloides; values unverified.
Song: rapid high twittering trill and 'chwit' notes; values unverified.
Reference: harsh chattering group calls; moved from Turdoides to Argya.
Song: high thin repeated 'tiu' notes amid flock twitter; formerly Paradoxornis.
Reference: rasping rising 'zhreee' call. Iberian birds are a separate species (C. cooki).
Reference: hoarse four-note coo, fundamental ~500 Hz; values fit.
Song: rambling warble with mimicry plus harsh notes; resident race stresemanni in New Guinea.
Song: long rambling mix of chatters, trills and whistles; values unverified.
Song: sizzling buzzy chatter ending in swizzle; values unverified.
Reference: soft bubbling 5-7 note coo; long-established introduced population around Perth, WA.
Reference: harsh 'chirr' and 'tsik' flock calls; values unverified.
Song: chirruping 'chissip-chirrup' series; values unverified.
Song: ringing whistled 'wee-te-tee' phrases; race harterti resident in SW Arabia.
Genus Crinifer (IOC/Clements). Reference: drawn-out nasal 'g-waaay', harmonic, low.
Reference: tremulous whinnying whistle; Clements lumps in Black Kite; race arabicus in SW Arabia.
Reference: harsh clattering 'kek-kek-kaaa' cackle; values unverified.
Reference: strident ringing 'kree-kreeip' calls; values unverified.
Reference: wailing 'aah-aah-aaaah' with dying fall; corvid-typical values fit.
Reference: antiphonal 'pee-wee' duet of loud ringing mid-pitched whistles.
Song: rich low piping whistles; Cracticus song notes mostly ~0.7-2.5 kHz.
Reference: bell-like piping contact whistles; values unverified.
Reference: rapid 'pi-pi-pi' piping and rising whistles; values unverified.
Reference: harsh 'carrak' flight call (males also pipe); values unverified.
Song: extended mimicry sequences plus own territorial phrases; broadband.
Reference: sharp metallic 'chik' notes and chatter; values unverified.
Reference: raucous coughing 'chock-chock' calls; values unverified.
Song: bell notes mixed with clicks, wheezes, gurgles. Wikipedia title is Tūī; 'Tui' is ambiguous.
Song: liquid chiming bell-like phrases; values unverified.
Reference: loud metallic 'keh-keh-keh'; resident in Panama/Costa Rica, spreading north.
Reference: soft low Mourning Dove-like coo, weak harmonics; resident in Lesser Antilles.
Song: thin, sibilant buzzy trill, little energy below ~4 kHz.

Song: chip notes and short phrases; introduced, established in Jamaica, Puerto Rico, Panama, Hawaii. [merge: au dropped — Hawaii/Pacific-island-only populations lie outside the app’s au realm (Australia, NZ, New Guinea)]
Song: loud accelerating shrill duet series; values unverified.
Reference: raucous 'raaa-ak' screech; native range reaches eastern Panama.
Song: explosive metallic 'bock' and 'tink' series, impulsive/percussive; values unverified.
Reference: harsh 'chee-chee-chee' chatter; values unverified.
Song: loud varied phrases with mimicry, like Northern Mockingbird.
Song: rich loud whistled phrase; Saltator songs centre ~2.5-3.5 kHz.
